Improve the space you already have

Renovation modernizes an existing interior while protecting the parts that still work.

Woodex audits the condition first, then plans the right mix of layout changes, services, finishes, joinery and furniture. When the space stays occupied, the work is sequenced by room, floor or working hours.

Built around occupancy

The renovation process in ten clear steps

Scope, cost and phasing are documented before site work begins.

Plan an assessment
Step 01

Site Survey & Condition Audit

Measure, photograph and identify what must be replaced or retained.

Evidence before scope
Step 02

Goals, Budget & Timeline

Clarify the result, what must stay, budget range and target date.

A practical brief
Step 03

Scope & Feasibility

Define every area, trade and phased work zone.

Nothing assumed
Step 04

Design & 3D

Resolve layouts, materials and renders where design is included.

See it before site
Step 05

Itemized BOQ

Price the renovation trade by trade and room by room.

Transparent cost plan
Step 06

Contract & Programme

Agree milestones, payments and the occupancy plan.

Phasing documented
Step 07

Strip-Out & Repair

Remove old work and prepare structure and surfaces.

Controlled disruption
Step 08

MEP First-Fix

Complete electrical, plumbing, HVAC and data work.

Services coordinated
Step 09

Finishes & Joinery

Install flooring, ceilings, walls, furniture and built-ins.

The new space takes shape
Step 10

Snagging & Handover

Inspect, correct, clean and formally hand over the space.

Ready to use

What Woodex can upgrade

Every trade is selected around durability, budget and the approved BOQ.

  • Raised access flooring

Surfaces & finishes

  • Porcelain, vinyl, wood and epoxy flooring
  • Paint, texture, panels and wallpaper
  • Skirting and transitions
  • Acoustic treatment
  • Wet-area waterproofing

Services & furniture

  • Electrical and LED lighting
  • Plumbing and sanitaryware
  • HVAC and air conditioning
  • Custom counters, cabinets and wardrobes
  • Workstations and display furniture

Practical answers

Renovation FAQ

Renovation upgrades an existing space through layout changes, improved services, new finishes, joinery or furniture.

Renovation improves an existing interior. Fit-out completes a shell or unfinished space for first use.

Often, yes. Work can be phased room by room, floor by floor or outside normal operating hours.

Yes. The survey identifies what must be replaced and what can be retained or repaired.

It is included when the renovation needs a new design direction. Smaller refreshes may not require it.

An itemized BOQ sets out every trade, room and material before the renovation programme begins.

A focused refresh can take 1 to 3 weeks. A full home, floor or multi-zone project can take 4 to 10 weeks.
